facts.fact: The Kodiyur drying shed where off-duty night-guards meet is at the end of a lane behind the fish market, with three doors (front, side, and one behind the nets); the palace infirmary is said to have ears, so Thankam sees the guards there.
facts.why: needed because the beat sends Usha to a drying shed of off-duty guards.

facts.fact: Neela's five companions (Thilak, Pavi, Madhavi, Kuttu, Meenu) entered by the Salt Gate behind a pepper cart and wait in a salt store near the tanneries; Neela went in alone by the Hill Gate.
facts.why: needed to explain where the rest of the Kodiyur party is while Neela meets Usha.

facts.fact: Neela's disguise: green starched cotton cuffs pegged at the knuckle, and a throat paste of pass-village lime and potter's ochre that dries chalky; the wedding bangle sits under the left cuff.
facts.why: needed to show how she passes as one of the queen's own.

facts.fact: Rukmini sells dried mackerel at the third stall from the weighing house, with scale-boy Pappu.
Sajan (Second Guard) is a man, bitter about the queen; Lata (Third Guard) is a woman loyal to the queen whose brother's wife received a death-gift reply; Sanu (Fourth Guard) is the youngest.
facts.why: named in the beat; characterisation added.

facts.fact: Sanu carried the notes for a year, given by a man in a grey cloak in the lower court who 'counted' him each time and never spoke; Sanu never read them.
facts.why: detail for Sanu's confession; echoes the grey-cloaked household figure.

facts.fact: Usha says the sea-stair landing guard change is at the sixth bell, takes sixty breaths, and leaves the landing empty for the last twelve (nine if it is blowing).
facts.why: gives the sea-stair timing the beat requires Usha to know exactly.

facts.fact: Chathu has been asking for Seventeen for three days, saying she would come.
facts.why: sets up the chapter's closing line and ch 13.
